adjudications.topic: (d) «नया» carries both 'new' and 'newer' — acceptable without a comparative?
adjudications.verdict: PASS — acceptable; no comparative is available and none is needed here
adjudications.reasoning: Four reasons, in order of weight. (1) Hindi has no usable comparative of this adjective: नएतर is not a word, and इससे नया ('newer than it') requires an antecedent that these strings deliberately do not have. (2) The catalogue already uses नया for the fresh re-read (account_failed नया सत्यापन, quote_unread नया खाता और कोट), so one carrier is this locale's established register rather than a compression. (3) The wrong reading is blocked structurally, not lexically: 'this device's new sign-in' is the possessive इस डिवाइस के, which makes the sign-in an artifact the device already holds (a sign-in the user would perform reads इस डिवाइस पर नया साइन-इन), and the verb throughout is जोड़ें ('join/reconnect'), never साइन इन करें. (4) The referent is provably unique: local_operator/providers/account_successor.py requires exactly one enabled, non-dead same-account row on the same hub before it re-points, so 'the new one' and 'the newer one' are the same row in every state where this plan is offered. The residual risk is that the title read alone loses 'newer'; that is a nuance, not a wrong instruction, and the remedy restores it immediately with पहले से … मौजूद है.

observations_outside_this_delta: At the TUI notice's real body width (74 cells at 80 columns) the remedy wraps to 2 rows and the receipt fits one; Devanagari is measured with the product's own `cell_len`, the same measure Textual lays out with, so these are the rows that paint. Glyph shaping (conjunct rendering in the user's terminal) is the terminal's job and is not claimed here.
`mobile.setup` is not a `wire.*` namespace, so these strings never reach the phone client's bundled chunks; the surfaces are the CLI/TUI notice and the desktop remedy paragraph.

findings.string: …इस डिवाइस के नए साइन-इन से… / एक नया साइन-इन…
findings.issue: «नया» carries 'new', 'newer' and 'fresh' in this catalogue, so the English comparative 'newer' loses its comparative form. Read alone, the title could be taken as 'this device's new sign-in' rather than 'the newer of the two local sign-ins'.
findings.assessment: Acceptable, and no better form exists. Hindi has no usable comparative of this adjective (नएतर is not a word; इससे नया needs an antecedent the strings do not have), the catalogue already uses नया for the fresh re-read, the possessive इस डिवाइस के plus पहले से … मौजूद है fix the referent, the verb is जोड़ें ('join/reconnect') and never साइन इन करें, and account_successor.py guarantees exactly one candidate row, so 'the new one' and 'the newer one' are the same row. The residual loss is a nuance in the title, not a wrong instruction. See adjudication (d).

findings.status: accepted — no change; note for a future wave
findings.string: साइन-इन (hyphenated) vs साइन इन (spaced) elsewhere in the namespace
findings.issue: The namespace ships «साइन-इन» in title_login, identity_unavailable and these three keys, and «साइन इन» in login, complete, complete_tui and login_tui. Two spellings in one namespace can read as drift.
findings.assessment: The split is grammatical, not accidental: the hyphenated form is the compound NOUN (Radient साइन-इन चाहिए, साइन-इन किए गए खाते), and the spaced form is the verb phrase (साइन इन करें / साइन इन करने). These three keys use the noun, so they belong on the hyphenated side — the same side as the title ledger they extend. No change. A future hi wave should record the noun/verb split in the style guide so the next translator does not read it as drift and 'unify' it.
